review_type: Qualitative fact inspection of retained whole-stream ASR transcripts; not a benchmark or human listening score

summary.baseline_observation: All five whole-stream transcripts contain acknowledgement, airport navigation started, and 88-minute ETA.
summary.correction_observation: All five contain acknowledgement, deliberately interrupted old Navigation to fragment, correction acknowledgement, navigation to the office/Tech Park, and previous airport destination replaced.
summary.unexpected_content: No additional route action or contrary destination is present in these ASR outputs; this does not establish physical audibility or rule out unrecognized speech.
summary.phonemizer_interpretation: The live worker logged one words-count mismatch warning during each baseline trial and two during each correction trial, within nonoverlapping trial windows. All expected complete-result fact phrases were recognized despite these warnings. Proper-name spellings differ consistently. The warning text alone neither identifies omitted words nor establishes the cause of those differences.

limitations: No human listener reviewed these recordings; recognition is an intelligibility proxy.
The production ASR model is reused, so ASR spelling errors and TTS pronunciation errors cannot be separated.
Warnings lack room/speech identifiers; association is by timestamp inside sequential, nonoverlapping trial windows, not a TTS request ID.
The interrupted old result is intentionally partial. Its absent airport completion and ETA are not complete-result failures.
Whole-stream transcripts do not establish the time of each spoken word, absence of PCM after a cancellation, or physical speaker playout.
Concatenated capture samples retain silence present in received frames but do not reconstruct gaps where frames were not delivered.
No clips were excluded, trimmed, retried, or selected according to recognized content.
